content.comment_body: With my [article_no] module, set to a static IP address in the USA, I can monitor the base module via its webserver on my Windows 10 PC or any Android smartphone. My mobile provider is AT&T, and I always have reliable 4G LTE coverage. However, when using Safari on iPhone or iPad, I can only see the module’s virtual display if the device is on WiFi; otherwise, the display remains blank. This issue occurs with multiple iPhones and iPads. Before I consult an Apple technician, is there a setting I might be overlooking?

I tested this with one of my own devices and noticed it doesn't work if I only enter the IP address. But if I include 'http://' before the IP address, for example, http://147.149.225.200, then it works properly.

analysis.insight_summary: Users found that access to a [product_name] module's webserver works reliably on Windows PCs and Android devices, but access fails on iPhones and iPads if connected via cellular data—the display stays blank. This affects multiple iOS devices regardless of network strength. Some users discovered that explicitly specifying 'http://' before the IP address enables access on iOS devices.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward web access to the [product_name] module's display from iOS devices over both WiFi and cellular connections, without needing any extra configuration or workaround.
